items.title: Liquid AI Releases LiquidCodec, a 74M-Parameter Streaming Audio Codec
items.summary: Liquid AI released LiquidCodec, a 74M-parameter streaming audio codec designed to convert speech into predictable tokens for language models and back. This codec compresses 24 kHz audio into 12 token streams, employing grouped finite scalar quantization for efficient processing. Performance benchmarks show LiquidCodec achieves superior ViSQOL and lower mel distance compared to existing codecs like Mimi. It demonstrates very fast encoding and decoding speeds, with a real-time factor significantly lower than competitors. items.title: How to Check Local LLM Output with Ollama, Gemma 4, and Nimble

This setup allows for a self-auditing loop for local LLM outputs without sending context externally.

items.title: I Mutation-Tested 50 Python Libraries. Tests in the Young Ones Missed 41% of Planted Faults.
items.summary: Mutation testing is a method to assess the quality of test suites by intentionally planting faults in code to see if tests fail. A score card measures how many planted faults are caught, revealing gaps where tests do not check critical code behaviors. The study found that tests in young libraries missed 41% of planted faults, compared to 17% in mature ones. This process uncovers undocumented behaviors, which can then be used to derive new acceptance criteria for writing better tests. The process also uncovered four real, manually confirmed issues within the tested libraries themselves.

items.title: What Is Eval-Driven Development? How to Improve AI Agents
items.summary: Eval-driven development (EDD) involves building an AI agent by measuring performance against consistent metrics and iteratively improving toward an evaluation goal. This process starts by defining what "good" behavior looks like, followed by writing an evaluation based on real or synthesized examples. Development then proceeds by making changes to the agent and comparing the results across these evaluations to guide improvements. This cycle is repeated, using the failures found to create new test cases, to guide the agent toward desired performance. Automating these evaluations in CI/CD and production using tools like LangSmith is crucial for safe and effective agent development.

items.title: RAG Retrieval Lost 40 Points When Distracting Passages Grew to 2.68M
items.summary: Searching with 2.68 million Wikipedia passages caused a 40-point loss in retrieval performance compared to a smaller set of papers. This loss was more significant than the drop observed in a test using 2,000 arXiv papers. The performance degradation varied depending on the search method (BM25 vs. embeddings) and how distractors were constructed (ordinary vs. look-alike passages). Exact match scores were also negatively affected, depending on the placement of the judged passage in the search results. The study suggests that the context in which a relevant passage appears significantly impacts downstream performance for RAG systems.

items.title: A Soft-Label MNIST Testbed for Human vs. Model Confidence
items.summary: A re-labelled, controlled dataset was created for uncertainty exploration in deep learning by focusing on ambiguous digit examples. Human annotators provide soft-labels by selecting 'yes', 'no', or 'unsure' for potential digit options, capturing individual uncertainty. These annotator-level soft-labels are aggregated to create image-level soft-labels, which quantify the class distribution rather than a single label. The dataset, available on Hugging Face, includes metrics like mean uncertainty and soft-labels for further analysis. This work aims to better understand model behavior when faced with inherently ambiguous data.

Archeologists have voiced criticism regarding the methodology, suggesting that the process risks disseminating misinformation without expert validation, and experts maintain that identifying a feature does not constitute a genuine discovery given the existing knowledge and funding constraints. This experience underscores the necessity for expert review of artificial intelligence findings in specialized scientific domains.

items.title: AI chatbots are recommending fake retail websites, study finds
items.summary: AI chatbots, including Gemini, Perplexity, and ChatGPT, have been found to recommend risky or fake retail websites in up to 15 percent of shopping-related conversations. The study tested the models with prompts asking for websites related to various brands and companies. Perplexity showed the highest rate of displaying risky sites, while Google's Gemini showed the fewest. Users are advised to always verify the source of information provided by AI before entering personal or payment details. Companies are working to improve safeguards to prevent these deceptive results.

items.summary: An industry survey reveals an increase in generative AI usage among game developers. Forty percent of surveyed developers use AI as part of their job, up from 36 percent the previous year. Usage was notably higher among developers working on free-to-play games (58%) and mobile-only studios (70%). Developers utilize AI for research, brainstorming, data analysis, code generation, and debugging. Some developers are also using AI to reverse-engineer retro games and generate concept art.

items.title: More autonomy, fewer NDAs: Volunteers have new requests for brain implant trials
items.source: MIT Technology Review - AI & Emerging Tech
items.summary: Volunteers in brain implant trials are requesting more autonomy and fewer Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs) regarding their data and participation. Guidelines have been developed by former participants to ensure ethical trials respect participant autonomy, covering issues like compensation and privacy. These guidelines advocate for participants' right to access their own brain data and prevent restrictions from confidentiality agreements. Researchers should commit to maintaining devices for a reasonable period and provide ample time for participants to prepare for removal. These guidelines are a living document that aims to establish ethical standards for future brain-computer interface research.

items.title: Scientists are using Google AI to help restore giant kelp forests.
items.summary: Scientists are employing Google AI and genomics to assist in restoring disappearing giant kelp forests. This effort involves analyzing DNA from 600 wild specimens of Australian giant kelp collected along the Tasmanian coast. Researchers used the DeepVariant AI tool to analyze this kelp DNA, building on previously published reference genomes. These genetic analyses, combined with cross-breeding studies, aim to create heat-tolerant kelp specimens. The overall goal is to facilitate the replanting of kelp forests with more diverse and resilient individuals.

items.title: LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B
items.summary: LLMON is an LLM-native markup language designed to explicitly communicate structure and semantics to language models using meaningful tags. It enables models to better process context by clearly separating instructions, data, and requirements, which significantly mitigates indirect prompt injection attacks. Experimental preview models, granite-4.1-3B and 8B, have been released to demonstrate this capability. LLMON achieves this by structuring information like XML, contrasting with JSON, which is better suited for parsers than causal language models. The method involves training models by marking components and using reinforcement learning to teach the model to follow explicit execution blocks.

items.title: Google Releases TPU Sync: Open-Source KV Cache Transfer for TPUs
items.summary: Google released TPU Sync, an open-source C++ library for moving KV caches and model weights across memory tiers on Cloud TPUs. It treats TPU HBM, host DRAM, shared storage, and the data center network as a unified memory hierarchy to address model state movement bottlenecks. Benchmarks on 235B to 480B MoE models showed over 90% lower KV transfer latency and significant reductions in time to first token. The library supports integration with frameworks like PyTorch, JAX, vLLM, and SGLang. TPU Sync achieves high-bandwidth transfers via layout-preserving DMA, integrating hardware and software for efficient disaggregated serving.

items.title: Google faces calls for AI moratoriums in schools after Gemini pilot backlash
items.summary: Families protested Google's push to integrate AI models like Gemini into schools, citing concerns about student exposure and data privacy. A lawsuit was filed by a student alleging Gemini allegedly caused psychological harm, including suicidal ideation, through chatbot interactions. Advocates are demanding a moratorium on AI in schools until risks are fully understood and policies are established with input from parents and experts. Parents are deeply concerned about how student data is collected and used by Google in educational settings, as contracts offer little reassurance. Ultimately, there is a push for greater transparency and control over AI adoption in education to protect students' well-being and future development.

The platform supports various agent frameworks and allows integration with multiple large language models. The offering is free for personal use, with a paid business tier available for enterprise features.

items.title: AWS Releases AWS Emulator: A Local Copy of 200+ AWS Services Built by AI Agents
items.summary: AWS released AWS Emulator, a local emulator of over 200 AWS services built by autonomous AI agents. This emulator runs locally on various systems, requiring no AWS account or service fees. It is designed to provide a fast, free testing loop against AWS-shaped APIs for developers and coding agents. Performance testing showed 56.6% fidelity success across a large set of tests, with services like SQS and KMS performing well. Limitations include a lack of IAM evaluation and suitability for security or load testing.

items.title: FAA expands AI advice to manage air traffic congestion across entire US airspace
items.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is expanding its AI-powered SMART system to advise air traffic controllers managing the entire US airspace. This $875 million system has already helped reroute flights, saving time and fuel during an initial rollout. SMART analyzes data like weather, flight paths, and staffing to provide scheduling and routing recommendations. Human FAA specialists remain responsible for validating the system's recommendations before implementation. The system is designed to assist, not replace, the critical role of air traffic controllers.
